subject: Operator simulations & resilience evidence for isolated deployment
messages:
From: Emma Ross <emma.ross@customershift.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Evidence request — operator simulations for air-gapped run

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As part of our regulatory review (we're finalizing a control set for an upcoming audit), our security team needs artifacts that show how Redwood validates operator procedures and resilience in isolated/offline deployments. Can you provide: 

- A short summary of operator simulation exercises you run for air-gapped installs (what you test, frequency, who runs them)
- Any runbooks used during a simulated outage (operator steps, failover/fallback actions)
- Results/metrics from the most recent simulation (time-to-recovery, replication lag, operator error rate)

We're aiming to include these as Exhibit B in our procurement packet. If you have anything redacted or a summary PDF that's fine — just need enough detail for our auditors.

Appreciate it — can we get something by next Wednesday (3/28)?

Best,
Emma
Emma Ross
Head of Security & Compliance
CustomerShift Inc.

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Emma Ross <emma.ross@customershift.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 11:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request — operator simulations for air-gapped run

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise package that should address your auditors' questions: operator-simulation-summary.pdf (3 pages) and resilience-runbook.md (operator playbook excerpt). High level notes here in case you want quick answers: 

- Who runs them: our Site Reliability team (private deployments) with an independent observer from Product Security, quarterly cadence for production-equivalent installs, monthly for newly provisioned environments.
- Scope: operator access procedures, KMS/secret handoff, controlled shutdown/startup, KV cache rehydration, model weights integrity checks, network reattachment and DNS/route re-stitch, backup restore timing.
- Metrics from last simulated outage (Feb 2028 simulation): mean time-to-recover network+runtime: 28 min; operator manual step completion median: 3.8 min/step; number of manual rollback actions: 0; KV cache warm-up to steady-state tokens/sec: ~95% of baseline after 42 minutes.

Notes on redaction: we removed customer-identifying IDs and shortened internal-check logs — auditors usually accept the summary plus a signed attestation from Redwood security. If your team needs the full CSV log from the Feb run, we can provide it under an NDA or a redacted version.

I've CC'd Vanessa and Jonas to confirm the metrics and to attach the network isolation test artifact if you want it.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachment: operator-simulation-summary.pdf (summary, redacted logs)
Attachment: resilience-runbook.md (excerpt)

Soojin — forwarding the thread with a couple notes before we send the CSV artifact: 

- Feb run log CSV contains timestamps and operator account IDs; we'll scrub per Emma's request (replace operator email -> role identifiers).
- Network isolation test report (we ran a multi-point isolation on 2028-02-14) includes packet capture summaries — provide as a condensed CSV with pass/fail columns rather than full pcap blobs.
- Suggest we include a short attestation paragraph from Security (me or Jonas) stating the simulation governance: scope, observer, ticketing references.

I'll prepare the cleaned artifacts and the attestation. Jonas, can you confirm the KMS integration screencast pointer is safe to share as a view-only recording?

-Vanessa

Subject: Re: Evidence request — operator simulations for air-gapped run

Emma — following up with the deeper artefacts Vanessa mentioned. I've attached the network-isolation-test-report.csv (condensed) and linked a short recorded demo of the KMS handoff we use in private installs. A few implementation clarifications: 

- KMS handoff: we require a customer-controlled KMS for private/on-prem installs; our operator playbook includes an HSM-based unseal procedure. The screencast demonstrates the operator-triggered unwrap and the client-side confirmation handshake — no secrets leave the customer's KMS.
- Operator simulations include an independent observer (Product Security) and a post-mortem ticket created in our tracking system — we provide ticket IDs in the redacted logs for traceability.
- Recovery windows: the 28-min mean recovery above is for a standard model shard restart with KV cache rebuild. For full control-plane+edge-network outage the worst-case measured in staged sim was 73 minutes (this is the outlier test with full rehydrate and model checksum verification).

If your auditors want a signed attestation form, Vanessa is prepared to sign; otherwise the attached CSV + runbook excerpt plus the screencast link should satisfy most evidence requests.

Link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kms-demo-view-only

Regards,
Jonas Weber
Senior Infrastructure Engineer — Redwood Inference

Attachments: network-isolation-test-report.csv (summary), kms-integration-screencast.mp4 (view-only reference)

We'll include the documents in Exhibit B. Vanessa — can we get the signed attestation as a PDF (simple one-paragraph statement) by EOD Thursday? That will close this item on our side.

Once that's done I'll share a quick note to procurement to move the contract to legal. Thanks for the quick turnaround — this was very helpful.

Emma
